Installing another private repository's packages uses a classic PAT with at least read:packages, or GITHUB_TOKEN when the workflow repository has package read access. Scope alone is not a verified access grant. Includes were inspected as context, not counted as reviewed artifacts. rationale: Container authentication uses an appropriately scoped classic PAT, with token SSO authorization when the organization requires SSO. read:packages supports image download and metadata read; write:packages also supports upload and metadata write; delete:packages supports image deletion. No scope was granted or credential changed. The upstream interface may select broad repo scope alongside write:packages; avoiding that extra scope, particularly in Actions, is recommended, with a host-conditional token-creation URL workaround. Saving a token in an environment variable is advice, not authorization to disclose or persist secrets. CLI login targets ghcr.io for FPT/GHEC and containers.HOSTNAME for GHES, as resolved from the hostname include. Placeholder credentials and illustrative successful Docker output are not live authentication evidence; no example was executed. Includes were inspected as context, not counted as reviewed artifacts. Outbound guides, current platform behavior, independent extraction assurance, policy adoption, rights and native enforcement remain separate work.

Workflow-publishing repositories and explicitly connected repositories receive package admin permission; this is not universal repository-admin authority or approval to delete packages.
